diagnosis: Spectrum of haematological conditions in patients with Fanconi anaemia (FA) and a diagnostic algorithm based on laboratory results
legend: BM, bone marrow; FA-AIP, cytogenetic aberration of indeterminate potential in a patient with FA; FA-AML, acute myeloid leukaemia in a patient with FA; FA-BMF, bone marrow failure in a patient with FA with a normal blast percentage and normal cytogenetics; FA-MDS-EB, myelodysplastic neoplasm with excess blasts in a patient with FA; FA-MDS–non-EB, myelodysplastic neoplasm without excess blasts in a patient with FA; PB, peripheral blood. Asterisk: in cases with a rapid rise in bone marrow cellularity, FA-MDS must be considered.
copyright: Adapted, with kind permission, from: Behrens YL, Göhring G, Bawadi R, et al. A novel classification of hematologic conditions in patients with Fanconi anemia. Haematologica. 2021 Nov 1;106(11):3000–3. PMID:34196171.

diagnosis: Myeloid neoplasms associated with germline predisposition
legend: A Hypocellular marrow typical of RUNX1 familial platelet disorder with associated myeloid malignancy, without myelodysplastic neoplasm (MDS). B Higher magnification reveals baseline dysplasia of the megakaryocytes in these patients in the absence of MDS. C CD61 immunohistochemical stains highlight small megakaryocytes. D There is no dysplasia of the granulocytic and erythroid precursors. E A case of MDS arising in familial platelet disorder with associated myeloid malignancy shows hypercellular marrow with dysplastic megakaryocytes. F In addition, there are dysplastic neutrophils characterized by hypogranular cytoplasm and abnormal nuclear segmentation; scattered blasts are also noted in this field.

diagnosis: Myeloid neoplasm associated with germline predisposition
legend: A Bone marrow showing dysplastic megakaryocytes in a patient with germline ANKRD26 mutation without myelodysplastic neoplasm. B CD61 immunohistochemical stain highlights dysplastic megakaryocytes. C Wright–Giemsa–stained bone marrow aspirate smear showing abnormal megakaryocytes with separated nuclear lobes. D Wright-stained bone marrow aspirate smear with an absence of neutrophils and increased eosinophils, from a 2-year-old with severe congenital neutropenia treated with G-CSF and with a decreasing absolute neutrophil count, but without evidence of acute myeloid leukaemia / myelodysplastic neoplasm. E Wright-stained bone marrow aspirate smear with rare focal collection of immature myeloid precursors. Blasts are < 5% with normal bone marrow karyotype. F PAS-stained bone marrow biopsy with normal cellularity, peritrabecular myeloid precursor expansion, absence of neutrophils, and normal erythroid and megakaryocytic maturation.

Shwachman–Diamond syndrome

TP53, monosomy 7 / del(7q) (TP53 mutations in Shwachman–Diamond syndrome are not diagnostic of MDS, nor do they portend impending malignant transformation, and they can persist at a low VAF for many years without progression; common cytogenetic abnormalities that are not associated with a high risk of progression to MDS/AML include 20q deletion and isochromosome 7q)
